name: Conflict and interference tasks
scope: A task-relevant feature must be reported while a task-irrelevant feature of the same stimulus or of a distractor pulls toward a competing response; the cost on incongruent trials is the measure.

name: Response inhibition and stopping tasks
scope: A prepared or prepotent response must be withheld or cancelled on a minority of trials; commission errors and stopping latency are the measures.

name: Attentional cueing and orienting tasks
scope: A cue precedes a target and predicts its location or identity with some validity; the benefit of valid over invalid cues is the measure.

name: Visual search and tracking tasks
scope: A target must be found among, or followed through, a field of distractors; search slopes, detection accuracy or tracking capacity are the measures.

name: Oddball, vigilance and continuous performance tasks
scope: A long stream of stimuli contains rare targets or deviants; detection, false alarms, response variability or the evoked response to the rare event are the measures.

name: Perceptual judgment and psychophysics tasks
scope: A judgment about a sensory stimulus near or below threshold, or a passive presentation designed to isolate a perceptual response; thresholds, accuracy and evoked responses are the measures.

name: Short-term and working memory tasks
scope: A small set of items must be held, and sometimes manipulated, over a delay of seconds before a probe or reproduction; span, capacity or set-size effects are the measures.

name: Recall and recognition memory tests
scope: A study phase is followed, after minutes or longer, by a test that asks the participant to recall, recognize or attribute studied material; hits, false alarms and their decomposition are the measures.

name: Memory control and prospective memory tasks
scope: Encoding or retrieval is deliberately shaped by instruction: an item is to be forgotten, suppressed, related to the self, or an intention is to be executed later; the effect on later memory or on intention completion is the measure.

name: Metacognition, agency and interoception tasks
scope: The participant reports on their own cognition, action or body: confidence in future recall, the perceived time of an action, the sense that a limb or heartbeat is theirs; the correspondence between report and fact is the measure.

name: Conditioning, reinforcement and implicit learning tasks
scope: Contingencies between stimuli, actions and outcomes are learned from experience, with or without explicit instruction; learning curves, choice probabilities and perseveration are the measures.

name: Motor performance and speeded response tasks
scope: Movement itself is the object: timing, sequencing, adaptation or speed of a well-specified response; tapping rate, error, completion time and dual-task cost are the measures.

name: Rule use, planning and reasoning tasks
scope: A rule must be discovered, applied, switched or used to plan a sequence of moves; switch costs, perseverative errors, solution accuracy and planning time are the measures.

name: Reward, risk and value-based choice tasks
scope: Options differing in reward magnitude, probability, delay or effort are chosen between, or a cue announces a potential reward before a speeded response; choice curves and anticipatory responses are the measures.

name: Social cognition and social choice tasks
scope: Another agent's mental state must be inferred, or money must be allocated between the participant and another player; inference accuracy and allocation patterns are the measures.

name: Emotion elicitation and regulation tasks
scope: Affective stimuli are presented to elicit, recognize or regulate an emotional response; ratings, physiological responses and recognition accuracy are the measures.

name: Language comprehension and production tasks
scope: Words, sentences or pictures are read, heard, named or generated; reading time, naming latency, lexical decision speed and fluency counts are the measures.

name: Spatial cognition and navigation tasks
scope: A location or orientation in space must be learned, imagined or found; path efficiency, rotation cost and spatial errors are the measures.

name: Pseudo tasks: rest, fixation, self-report and feedback blocks
scope: Block-level activities that serve the experiment around them rather than eliciting a process through trials: a resting block as a baseline or a reset, a fixation block that sets up a physical state, a questionnaire that collects a self-report, and feedback that tells the participant how they are performing, after a response, a block or a session. For rest, fixation and questionnaires the block's onset, offset and instruction are what is recorded; for feedback its schedule, content, valence and modality are recorded as well. Pseudo tasks have no process links recorded at this time.
